newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - APRIL 22.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Today's presentation of the Bank of Greece's annual report on the course of the economy is expected to focus on the need for the immediate taking of structural measures to support and boost growth. While there is progress on the inflation and interest rates fronts, Governor Lucas Papademos is expected to point out the worrying developments in the balance of payments.

--Another six-seven insurance companies may face the revocation of their licences following the Insurance Firms Reserve Capital's decision to accept National Bank and Bank of Piraeus's offer of a 10 billion drachma loan. The loan will ease liquidity problems facing the reserve and will speed procedures to reform the market.
--The European Union is pressuring Greece anew on its taxation and regulations on the circulation of imported automobiles.

--Greece's telecoms organisation OTE share holders are in for a pleasant surprise with the final dividend per share rising to 180 drachmas from the 160 originally announced. Dividends are up 40 percent in 1996 over the profits for 1995, while the 1997 return for shareholders is expected to reach 250 drachmas per share.
IMERISIA

--The government intends to introduce drastic changes to the social security system as part of its efforts to curb tax evasion and recoup the 300 billlion drachmas lost annually by pension funds. Measures include the automatic imposition of fines and spot-checks in cooperation with the economic crimes squad, SDOE.
--Meanwhile, Labour and Social Security Minister Miltiades Papaioannou said yesterday that the government gave priority to getting employers to pay contributions to pension funds.

--Inflation for April is expected to note a further drop to 5.8 percent, while the rate for the end of the year is expected to settle at 4.39 percent, according to a recent study by Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis's office.
--The positive climate on the stock exchange is leading a number of listed firms to the capital market for share capital increases.
KERDOS

--According to reports, the European Commission's report on the Greek economy recognises the progress made over the past three years of its adherence to the convergence programme but stresses that the way forward must be found in privatisations, deregulation of the market and the strengthening of the taxation mechanism.

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou made overtures to US investors during his speech to 500 businessmen and investors in New York yesterday. Papandoniou stressed the opportunities available in Greece and the wider Balkan region for US investment.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Industrial production noted a significant increase of 0.8 percent in January this year, according to the National Statistics Service, indicating an auspicious start. Sources say however that the progress can only be built upon if public works and private construction activity maintain a positive course.

--The National Tourist Organisation EOT is optimistic about recent indications of an upturn in tourist arrival numbers for this year's season, with latest reports of a 20 percent increase in tourist arrivals from the US, and another 10 percent increase from Germany.
EXPRESS

--Despite the activation of the SDOE and its snap audits on firms and enterprises, tax revenues continue to remain at worryingly low levels, placing the successful execution of the state budget in serious doubt. Latest reports indicate that rates of increase for April will continue to be below those forecast in the budget, following the trend set since the beginning of the year.

--The Athens Stock Exchange was within reach of the 1,450 point mark on the general price index yesterday and appeared to be taking steady aim for the 1,500 mark. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
